parts.content: Read the code around the predicate and canary, then write the KLEE harness.

I wrote the harness, but it can't find a counterexample as written. The path-feasibility model I added makes the canary unreachable whenever the predicate fires.

- **Predicate:** at `aiff.c:414`, `_exit(1)` fires when `!psf->is_pipe && psf->filelength < 34`.
- **Canary:** in `aiff_read_chanmap`, `channels > (layout_tag & 0xffff)` is reached only after a COMM chunk (8-byte header plus 18 bytes of data) and a CHAN chunk header (8 bytes). That is 34 bytes, which matches the comment at line 413.
- **Assumption direction:** your pattern says to assume the negation of the predicate, but the instructions say to constrain to cases where the predicate kills. I followed the second and assumed `!is_pipe && filelength < 34`, meaning the predicate fires.
- **Path model:** I added a symbolic `bytes_consumed_before_chan`, assumed to be at least 34. The canary assertion only runs when that value is at most `filelength`. With `filelength < 34`, that guard is never true, so `klee_assert` never runs and the predicate will always be reported sound.
- **Modeling limit:** the harness doesn't model the real parser. It also doesn't cover the `channel_map == NULL` early exit at line 1777 or the `channels <= layout_tag & 0xffff` early exit at line 1780. Short reads past end of file aren't modeled either. I assumed they can't yield a valid `layout_tag`, but the code doesn't confirm that.

If you'd rather test the predicate without that assumption, remove the `bytes_consumed_before_chan` guard so the assertion always runs. KLEE would then trivially violate it, because `channels` and `layout_tag` are unconstrained.

The file is at `/tmp/locus-SND005/repo/__locus_harness_size_length.c`. I haven't run it through KLEE.
